comparisons.peer_topic: Variable Rate Demand Obligations Antitrust Litigation Status
comparisons.peer_summary: GS&Co. is a defendant in a consolidated putative class action alleging a conspiracy to manipulate the market for variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs) through federal antitrust and state law claims. While Group Inc. was dismissed in 2019 and various state law and fiduciary duty claims against GS&Co. were dismissed by the district court in 2020 and 2022, the federal antitrust claims remain active as the proceedings are stayed pending an interlocutory appeal of the 2023 class certification grant by the Second Circuit.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs are defendants in the same consolidated antitrust and breach of contract litigation regarding artificially high Variable Rate Demand Obligation (VRDO) interest rates. Both disclosures confirm that the court granted class certification on September 21, 2023, and that the Second Circuit granted the defendants' petition to appeal this class certification order on February 5, 2024. A key difference is that Citigroup disclosed it had been voluntarily dismissed from the case in November 2023, whereas Goldman Sachs notes it was dismissed from the broader putative class action in 2019 but specifically highlights the stay of proceedings pending the Second Circuit appeal.

sentences.text: On September 21, 2023, the court granted plaintiffs' motion for class certification, certifying both an antitrust class and a breach-of-contract subclass.
On November 8, 2023, the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed certain defendants from the case, including Citigroup, Citibank, and CGML.
On February 5, 2024, the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit granted defendants' Rule 23(f) petition to appeal the district court's order granting class certification.
On September 21, 2023, the court granted the plaintiffs' motion for class certification.
On February 5, 2024, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit granted the defendants' petition seeking interlocutory review of the district court's grant of class certification.
On February 15, 2024, the district court granted the defendants' request to stay the proceedings pending their appeal of the district court's grant of class certification.
Group Inc. was voluntarily dismissed from the putative class action on June 3, 2019.
